mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative whenever the trigger occurs, or the inflation-adjusted discount rate change is statistically insignificant.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 50,000 jobs and coincides with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be positive as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
regime_hint: Resilient labor market with low unemployment
failure_condition: In 20% of similar triggers, 60-day forward returns are negative or flat, or the interaction effect as measured by IC is below -0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 101.0 combined with a month-on-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to stronger supply-side momentum outweighing inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: Across 40+ similar events, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) while output momentum (INDPRO) remains flat or rising predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates a disinflationary soft landing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO >= previous month
failure_condition: In 30% of such events, 5-day forward returns are non-negative or the interaction effect IC > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent widening of the yield spread between 10-year Treasury and Fed Funds (implied by FEDFUNDS and long-term rates proxy GDPC1) predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns as higher real rates depress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: 10Y Treasury yield - FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 40 such windows, the 20-day forward return mean is positive or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC > 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (HOUST) exceeding 12,000 in a month while unemployment remains below 4% is associated with positive S&P 60-day forward returns as it signals labor market tightness and hiring momentum.
failure_condition: In 40% of such triggers, the 60-day forward return mean is negative or the interaction effect is weak (IC < -0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 253 combined with a rise in retail sales (PAYEMS) above 140,000 suggests a demand-side soft landing, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Across 50 such events, the forward return mean is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 3-month decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) with no change in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a supply-side shock, leading to negative S&P 20-day forward returns as market anticipates slower growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous 3 months AND INDPRO == previous month
regime_hint: Persistent inflation deceleration without output decline
failure_condition: In 60% of such events, forward returns are non-negative or the interaction effect IC > 0.05.
